title: Biggest funerals and multiple bands; Celestin and Buddy Petit funerals
summary: Clark recalls Henderson's funeral with five bands, recent two-band funerals, Celestin's funeral, and Buddy Petit's funeral with one scraped-up band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I'm wondering, change the subject a little, what was the biggest funeral you ever played with more bands, most bands and all? Well, I'll tell you, this Undertaker,

the Murray Henderson, he had five bands. That's what Kid Thomas told me the other day too. Five bands and the next one was old man Allen, he had four bands. I played both of those films. I just had to come into the Urica Band at that time. We had a bass player at that time by the name of Joe Howard. You heard of him? Used to be a trumpet player, but he paralyzed his lip when he went to bass. He paralyzed the nerve of his lip. He was making those high notes all the time, just just paralyzed his lip. He could play a nice bass player though. He made a nice bass player.
Well, how long has it been since you've played a funeral with more than one band?
Oh, it's been quite a while. A lot of this about a year or so. I believe you was on that last one when John Cashman was with us. I remember you had two bands. That's it. That's the last one I played.
How many did Celestan's funeral have? Three or?
Well, let me see. They had us, they had John,

and I think. Two fifteen men bands. That was the way it was. That's the way it was. But it was just two. Yeah, two or two. Thirty men in all. That's all. And they just added on to the band. That's right. That's right. Do you remember Buddy Petit's funeral?
Just one? I thought it was a great big...
You think of Kid Renee's? No. No.

They scrapped up a band for that funeral. Kid Howard scrapped up he and Ernest Rogers. Oh, right. And they went to a church down on Annette Street somewhere. And was it Annette? I think it was Annette. Annette or Lapa Roof somewhere. One of those streets downtown I know. Because Ernest called, come to me and asked me, would I go? I said, yeah, I'll go. By being a musician, you know, we all volunteered and went. And he had a nice funeral. Nice funeral.
No. They're taking him to the Baptist Church, I think it was.
